plan.title: Hallmark pathway activity per sample: UC inflamed vs control colon
plan.analytical_narrative:
The question asks for a per-sample pathway activity score and a hallmark heatmap that shows which pathways separate ulcerative colitis inflamed colon from control. The inputs are a 12,000 x 13 gene-level Salmon count CSV (/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv) and a 12 x 2 sample table (/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv), 6 UC inflamed vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch, human colon. No differential expression is requested, so the plan does not fit a gene-level contrast — it goes counts -> QC -> filter/normalize -> per-sample gene set scores -> heatmap and score-level test.

T1S1 runs the sample structure QC that the depth caveat makes mandatory: sample_01 has a library size about 4x below the median, and the rule of record is to keep it, inspect it on the PCA and the sample-distance heatmap, and report its library size and detected genes beside the others rather than deleting it silently. Removal, if any, must be argued in the report, not assumed. T1S2 filters to genes with at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples (the smallest group size) and produces the DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors and a blind VST matrix — normalization stays inside the count model, and the size factors are what protect the low-depth sample from biasing the scores.

T3S1 is the core answer: GSVA per-sample enrichment scores for the 50 MSigDB hallmark sets (human, HGNC symbols) on the VST matrix, giving one score per hallmark per sample, then limma on the score matrix under ~ condition with BH adjustment across the 50 sets, and the heatmap of hallmark scores across all 12 samples annotated by condition. GSVA is chosen over UCell/singscore here because the question is exactly the case the rule names for GSVA — many gene sets scored as one matrix across a fixed sample set, tested with limma. The stated cost of that choice is that a GSVA score is relative to the sample set, so the scores are not portable to new samples; the step must state this. Because gene symbols are the identifier space of the hallmark GMT, the step must report how many of the 50 sets survive the 12,000-gene matrix and how many member genes of each are present — a hallmark set with half its genes missing is a different set.

T2S2 adds an orthogonal, membership-free read: PROGENy footprint activity via decoupleR mlm on the top 500 responsive genes per pathway. This matters because a hallmark score is gene-set membership, which can move without the signalling pathway actually being engaged; the footprint score is the independent check on the inflammatory signalling (NFkB, TNFa, JAK-STAT) that hallmark will almost certainly flag in inflamed UC mucosa. It is supporting evidence, not the headline. T1S3 assembles the report with the reproducibility record.

Honest limits stated up front: n=6 per group with one low-depth sample; separation on a heatmap is descriptive, and the limma test on 50 scores is the inferential part. With 12,000 genes the matrix is likely pre-subset rather than a full transcriptome, so absolute hallmark coverage must be reported, and any hallmark set with fewer than ~10 members present should be dropped and named as dropped.

steps.method: blind VST, PCA on top variable genes, sample distance heatmap
keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least smallest group size of samples
DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors, VST matrix for scoring
GSVA per-sample scores on the 50 MSigDB hallmark sets with limma on the scores
decoupleR mlm on the PROGENy footprint model
reproducibility record and hallmark heatmap report

A heatmap of footprint activity across samples annotated by condition is produced, and per-pathway inflamed-vs-control differences are reported with BH adjustment
The report states the scores are footprints, not member-gene expression, and that no topology is used
constraints: activity_method = mlm (decoupleR multivariate linear model); ulm is the fallback estimator only
footprint_model = PROGENy human — match the organism, never the mouse model
top_responsive_genes = 500
Interpret and label as footprint, not membership
State that SPIA (topology-aware pathway impact) is absent from this environment and that no step here uses pathway topology
caveats: PROGENy covers roughly 14 signalling pathways — it is a narrow, mechanistic complement to the 50 hallmark sets, not a replacement for them
If the PROGENy weight model is not staged, this step is dropped without blocking the run; the research question is answered by T3S1
With 12 samples the per-pathway comparison is low-powered; treat concordance with hallmark as supporting evidence, not confirmation

grounding.reason: Pathway activity for a human count dataset: decoupleR mlm on the PROGENy footprint model with the top 500 responsive genes per R-0115@1504, read as a footprint; SPIA is the topology tool of record and is absent here, so the footprint model is the stated substitute per R-0122@08af. The STRING network setting of R-0123@5521 is carried but not exercised, since this plan runs no DE gene list to build a neighbourhood from.

steps.name: Report and reproducibility record
steps.question: Which hallmark pathways separate UC inflamed colon from control, how strong is that separation given 6 vs 6 and one low-depth sample, and what exactly was run?
steps.description: Assemble the final report: the QC verdict on sample_01 (library size, detected genes, position on PCA and hallmark clustering, retained or not and why), the hallmark score heatmap across the 12 samples as the headline figure, the ranked limma-on-scores table with BH-adjusted p-values naming which hallmark sets separate UC inflamed from control and in which direction, the PROGENy footprint result as corroboration or as an explicit skip, and the per-sample score tables. State the limits without softening them: n=6 per group, one sample at roughly a quarter of median depth, GSVA scores relative to this sample set, hallmark sets overlapping so hits arrive in correlated blocks, no pathway topology used anywhere, and no gene-level differential expression run (the question did not ask for one), so no claim about individual genes is supported. Attach the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, the random seed of every step that uses randomness, package versions, the hallmark collection version, the PROGENy model version, and the annotation release used for any symbol mapping.
steps.context: The user asked for a per-sample pathway score, a hallmark heatmap, and which pathways separate the groups. The report must deliver those three things and be explicit about what the 12-sample design can and cannot support.
acceptance_criteria: The hallmark heatmap across all 12 samples and the ranked BH-adjusted hallmark table are both included
The per-sample hallmark score table is delivered as a file
The low-depth sample_01 decision and any sensitivity check are stated
Limits are stated explicitly: sample size, GSVA sample-set dependence, hallmark set overlap, absence of topology, and absence of gene-level DE
Reproducibility record includes sessionInfo, seeds, package versions, and the hallmark collection version
constraints: Do not report a hallmark as separating the groups on heatmap appearance alone — pair every such claim with its BH-adjusted p-value
Do not make gene-level claims; no differential expression was run
caveats: A heatmap that looks clean at 6 vs 6 can still rest on a handful of samples; report the effect size alongside the p-value

grounding.reason: No rule covers the report step as such; the reproducibility record it carries follows R-0086@becf

flags.message: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

steps.method: blind VST, PCA on top variable genes, sample distance heatmap
keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least smallest group size of samples
DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors, VST matrix for scoring
GSVA per-sample scores on the 50 MSigDB hallmark sets with limma on the scores
decoupleR mlm on the PROGENy footprint model
reproducibility record and hallmark heatmap report
